page: Microsoft Azure M176ds_3_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine engineered for enterprise workloads demanding massive random-access memory footprints. Built on the x86_64 Intel architecture and managed by Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance features 176 dedicated virtual central processing units (vCPUs) combined with 2794.0 GB of system memory. This hardware allocation yields approximately 15.88 GB of RAM per vCPU, aligning with environments requiring high memory-to-core density.

Storage configuration includes 429 GB of direct-attached local solid-state drive (SSD) capacity, which is suited for temporary files, swap space, and fast scratch data. The instance supports Azure Premium Storage for persistent block volume attachments. Acceleration hardware is absent, as the system provides zero dedicated GPUs, directing all platform resources to memory and general CPU execution.

From an operational perspective, the M176ds_3_v3 offers consolidation efficiency by supporting massive single-node databases that would otherwise require multi-instance clustering. A notable architecture tradeoff is the relatively modest local SSD capacity when contrasted with the 2.8 TB memory footprint, necessitating reliance on remote storage for large persistent datasets. Best-fit workloads include large-scale in-memory databases, enterprise relational database management systems, and heavy extract-transform-load data processing pipelines.
